headline: Issued Negative Determination for 4 Gleason Street parking lot repaving and ratified beaver dam emergency certificate on Oaks View Street.
summary: The Conservation Commission continued several Notices of Intent and Violation cases to later meetings, including 11 Cross Street, 397 Transmission Line project, Brook Street Culvert, 143B Tyler Street, 28 West Street, 91 Lindbergh Ave, and 60 Ames Street. It approved a Negative Determination of Applicability for 4 Gleason Street parking lot repaving, ratified an emergency certificate for a beaver dam at 34, 36, 38 Oaks View Street, tabled a Certificate of Compliance for 175 Pelham Street, and voted to cancel the September 17, 2026 meeting.
decisions: Continued the Notice of Intent for 11 Cross Street (CROSSLD QOZB, LLC) to the July 16, 2026 meeting.
Continued the Notice of Intent for the 397 Transmission Line Asset Condition Refurbishment Project (BSC Group) to the July 16, 2026 meeting.
Continued the Notice of Intent for the Brook Street Culvert (TEC, Inc.) to the July 16, 2026 meeting.
Issued a Negative Determination of Applicability for the RDA at 4 Gleason Street (Methuen Village at Riverwalk).
Continued the Stormwater Management Permit for 11 Cross Street to the July 16, 2026 meeting.
Continued the Notice of Violation #26-006 for 143B Tyler Street to the August 20, 2026 meeting.
Continued the Notice of Violation #26-008 for 28 West Street to the August 6, 2026 meeting.
Continued the Notice of Violation #26-009 for 91 Lindbergh Ave to the July 16, 2026 meeting.
Continued the Notice of Violation #26-005 for 60 Ames Street to the August 20, 2026 meeting.
Ratified Emergency Certificate #26-0010 for the beaver dam at 34, 36, 38 Oaks View Street.
Tabled the Certificate of Compliance for 175 Pelham Street (MDRFL Realty LLC / Grieco Automotive Group).
Cancelled the September 17, 2026 meeting and moved continued items to the first October meeting.

plain_text:
CITY OF METHUEN 
CONSERVATION COMMISSION 
Minutes of a Meeting – July 2, 2026 
The City of Methuen Conservation Commission held a hybrid meeting via in-
person and Zoom video conferencing (VC) on July 2, 2026, at 7:00 p.m. at the 
alternate location of Sanborn Hall, 90 Hampshire Street, Methuen, MA 01844.  
Present for this meeting were Dave Di Zazzo, Chair; Kenneth Sateriale, 
Secretary; Sandra Boulay, Commissioner; and Patrice Friant, Commissioner.  
Also present were Conservation Officer Chris Parsons and Michelle Davidson, 
Conservation Clerk.   Absent were Cara Seaman, Vice Chair, and Rachel Lecher, 
Commissioner. 
Chairman Dave Di Zazzo announced that, pursuant to Chapter 20 of the Acts of 
2021, this meeting was conducted via remote means in accordance with 
applicable law.  Members of the public body, as well as members of the public, 
were able to access the meeting via virtual means through Zoom video 
conferencing.  In the event that access and participation were not achieved, 
the Commission would post on the City of Methuen website an audio or video 
recording, transcript, or other comprehensive record of proceedings as soon 
as possible after the meeting. 
I. NOTICES OF INTENT
Page 2 
A. Notice of Intent – DEP File #219-1320, MCC File #26-001 – 11 Cross 
Street – CROSSLD QOZB, LLC – Dresser, Williams & Way, Inc. 
(Continued from June 18, 2026) 
The applicant requested a further continuance to allow submission of an 
invasive species management plan and to address a pending waiver request 
for a 35-foot setback.  
MOTION: Motion made by Friant to continue to the July 16, 2026 meeting.  
Seconded by Sateriale.  Vote: Unanimous. 
B. Notice of Intent – DEP File #219-1321, MCC File #26-002 – 397 
Transmission Line Asset Condition Refurbishment Project – BSC Group 
(Continued from June 18, 2026) 
Hannah Raddatz (Wetland Scientist, BSC Group) presented responses to peer 
review comments from Lucas Environmental covering alteration fees, 
resource area identification, and structure replacements.  She explained that 
impacts to bordering land subject to flooding and buffer zones are temporary 
and restorative, and that structure replacements are exempt under the 
Wetlands Protection Act.  She noted that steel structures could last decades to 
over a century compared to wooden poles. 
Sateriale requested that all substantive assurances and responses be provided 
in writing before a vote is taken.  All commissioners agreed, citing proper 
record-keeping.  Ms. Raddatz agreed to submit a written memo addressing all 
open comments.  Davidson noted City Hall is closed Fridays and requested the 
memo be submitted by Tuesday morning.  The Commission confirmed 
acceptance of that deadline. 
MOTION: Motion made by Friant to continue to the July 16, 2026, meeting.  
Seconded by Sateriale.  All in favor. Vote: Unanimous. 
C. Notice of Intent – DEP File #219-1324, MCC File #26-005 – Brook 
Street Culvert – TEC, Inc. – Department of Public Works, City of Methuen
Page 3 
(Continued from June 18, 2026) 
The applicant requested a continuance to allow time for a peer review 
response to MassDEP comments. 
MOTION: Motion made by Friant to continue to the July 16, 2026 meeting.  
Seconded by Sateriale. All in favor.  Vote: Unanimous. 
II. CALL TO ORDER 
The official business meeting was called to order at 7:23 p.m. 
III. ACCEPTANCE OF AGENDA / AMENDMENTS (IF ANY) 
A clerical error was identified: the MCC number for the Notice of Violation at 
28 West Street was corrected to 26-008. 
MOTION: Motion made by Sateriale to accept the agenda as amended.  
Seconded by Boulay.  All in favor.  Vote: Unanimous. 
IV. ACCEPTANCE OF MINUTES – June 18, 2026 
MOTION: Motion made by Sateriale to accept the minutes of June 18, 2026.  
Seconded by Boulay.  All in favor.  Vote: Unanimous. 
V. NEW BUSINESS 
A. Request for Determination of Applicability (RDA) – 4 Gleason Street – 
Methuen Village at Riverwalk (MCC File #26-005) – Thomas Myers 
Tom Myers presented a request to replace existing asphalt in the parking lot 
at 4 Gleason Street.  The project is a like-for-like replacement with no changes 
to footprint, parking count (42 spaces, 4 handicapped), or square footage 
(approximately 32,976 sq ft).  The work is to be performed by EJ Paving, and 
reclaimed asphalt is to be disposed of at Brock Industries, Dracut, MA.  Mr. 
Myers confirmed EJ Paving is OSHA-trained and MassDOT-approved. 
Conservation Officer required 48-hour notice before erosion control 
installation for inspection, no stockpiling on site, and a bill of lading for 
reclaimed asphalt delivery to Brock Industries.  Mr. Myers confirmed EJ
Page 4 
Paving is aware of all conditions and will install erosion control prior to work 
commencement.  
MOTION: Motion made by Sateriale to issue a Negative Determination of 
Applicability (Negative 2 and 3, state and local) Seconded by Friant.  All in 
favor. Vote: Unanimous. 
VI. OLD BUSINESS 
A. Stormwater Management Permit – 11 Cross Street – CROSSLD QOZB, 
LLC – Dresser, Williams & Way, Inc. 
(Continued from prior meeting) 
This item was continued in conjunction with the associated Notice of Intent 
(Item I-A above). 
MOTION: Motion made by Friant to continue to the July 16, 2026 meeting.  
Seconded by Sateriale.  All in favor.  Vote: Unanimous. 
B. Notice of Violation #26-006 – 143B Tyler Street – Aaron DeGloria 
The property owner requested a continuance due to being out of town until 
August 20. 
MOTION: Motion made by Friant to continue to the August 20, 2026 meeting.  
Seconded by Sateriale.  All in favor. Vote: Unanimous. 
C. Notice of Violation #26-008 – 28 West Street – Harjinder Singh 
Conservation Officer discovered piles of fill on the property while driving by 
and issued a notice of violation.  Photos were presented to the commission.  
Issues include mounds of non-compliant fill, buried logs, an illegal drainage 
pipe, and fill near conservation markers. Garbage has been removed since the 
notice was issued, but logs and fill mounds remain. Some logs appear to have 
been buried.  Conservation markers are present; the exact setback (35 or 50 
feet) has not yet been confirmed, but the area is within the 100-foot 
jurisdictional zone.
Page 5 
Conservation Officer will meet with the property owner on-site on Tuesday to 
review Commissission remediation requirements, provide the ordinance on 
acceptable fill, and outline the required remediation actions.  Sateriale 
requested correction of the spelling of the property owner's name in the 
record: H-A-R-J-I-N-D-E-R S-I-N-G-H. 
Conservation Officer Parsons will meet with Mr. Singh on-site Tuesday July 7 
at 10:00 AM to review requirements and provide written ordinance guidance.  
Mr. Singh must remove non-compliant fill mounds and unbury any buried logs 
within the jurisdictional area. 
MOTION: Motion made by Friant to continue to the August 6, 2026 meeting.  
Seconded by Sateriale.  All in favor.  Vote: Unanimous. 
D. Notice of Violation #26-009 – 91 Lindbergh Ave – Lindbergh Ave, LLC 
The representative for the owner requested a continuance to July 16, 2026. 
MOTION: Motion made by Boulay to continue to the July 16, 2026 meeting.  
Seconded by Sateriale.  All in favor.  Vote: Unanimous. 
E. Notice of Violation #26-005 – 60 Ames Street – Muhammad Tasleem 
Muhammad Tasleem was previously issued a verbal cease and desist 
(followed by a written letter from the Commission that was hand-delivered by 
Parsons) for filling wetlands and dumping garbage.  Maureen Harold, Wet 
Land Scientist, working for Mr. Tasleem, conducted a delineation on Monday.  
The wetland line was confirmed approximately where Parsons previously 
estimated.  Loam was spread over the weekend on the non-wetland side of the 
property.  Remaining issues include garbage, logs, bricks, and other debris 
that must be removed by hand.  Erosion control markers are to be installed 
every 25 feet; the area is to be seeded for stabilization.  Wetlands are to be 
allowed to naturally regenerate.
Page 6 
Mr. Tasleem confirmed full cooperation from day one.  Sateriale commended 
the property owner's cooperation.  Parsons scheduled a site visit with Mr. 
Tasleem for Monday, July 6, at 2:30 PM. 
Mr. Tasleem was directed to remove all debris (garbage bags, logs, bricks) by 
hand, install erosion control markers every 25 feet, and seed the area for 
stabilization — all prior to the August 20, 2026 hearing. 
MOTION: Motion made by Friant to continue to the August 20, 2026 meeting. 
Seconded by Sateriale.  All in favor.  Vote: Unanimous. 
F. Emergency Certificate #26-0010 – 34, 36, 38 Oaks View Street (Beaver 
Dam) 
Conservation Officer Parsons issued an emergency certificate after receiving 
complaints from multiple residents about high water levels in their backyards 
caused by a beaver dam. The dam has been breached twice during the week; 
water levels were still elevated as of Wednesday.  The emergency certificate 
lasts 30 days.  Beavers have not been trapped in that locale in approximately 
two years.  Officer Parsons will continue breaching the dam as needed 
(approximately once or twice per week) within the 30-day emergency 
certificate period. 
MOTION: Motion made by Sateriale to ratify Emergency Certificate #26-0010.  
Seconded by Friant.  All in favor. Vote: Unanimous. 
G. Certificate of Compliance – 175 Pelham Street (DEP File #219-1315, 
MCC File #25-033) – MDRFL Realty LLC / Grieco Automotive Group 
The applicant has not responded to outreach from the Commission.  Two 
outstanding items remain on the plan to be completed by the applicant: a 
cement berm around a double catch basin and a hood for the outfall.  Two 
additional items were identified during site inspection: a 13,000-gallon 
exterior waste oil tank (approximately 50 feet from wetlands) and steel 
protective structures around the tank — neither of which are shown on the
Page 7 
plan.  No representative appeared at the meeting.  All four items must be 
reflected on the submitted plan and completed before compliance can be 
certified.  Parsons to communicate necessary actions to the applicant. 
MOTION: Motion made by Sateriale to table.  Seconded by Friant. All in favor. 
Vote: Unanimous. 
VII. CONSERVATION OFFICER'S REPORT 
Brown Court – Ongoing Violation (Informal Discussion) 
Conservation Officer Parsons reported an ongoing violation at Brown Court 
(at least one year).  The property owner has removed fill from the floodplain 
as required, leaving a depression approximately 20 by 30 feet and one foot 
deep.  The owner is requesting permission to install a riprap swale to prevent 
standing water and mosquito breeding.  The depression will hold water 
during rain events.  The owner plans to seed the area with grass mix and 
direct drainage flow toward the adjacent wetland via a small swale. 
Secretary Sateriale asked whether the engineering department should be 
involved given drainage flow and volume concerns.  Parsons noted 
engineering involvement is not typical for a project of this small scale but 
suggested that the Commission require the submission of an RDA as 
appropriate, given the owner's prior violation history.  
The Commission agreed that the property owner should be instructed to file 
an RDA application.  Officer Parsons will advise the Brown Court property 
owner to proceed with an RDA application as soon as possible. 
VIII. OTHER BUSINESS 
A. Administrative Announcements – Mandatory Furloughs and Schedule 
Changes 
Davidson informed the commission of mandatory City Hall furloughs — 
Fridays closed — for approximately 20 weeks, potentially through 
Thanksgiving, with reassessment after Labor Day.
Page 8 
Davidson announced that she will be on vacation and will not be at the 
September 17, 2026, meeting. 
MOTION: Motion made by Boulay to cancel the September 17, 2026, meeting 
and push any continued items to the first October meeting.  Seconded by 
Friant.  All in favor. Vote: Unanimous. 
Davidson will notify all relevant parties of the cancellation of the September 
17, 2026, meeting and rescheduling of continued items to the first October 
meeting. 
IX. ADJOURN 
There being no further business, a motion to adjourn was made by Sateriale 
and seconded by Friant.  All in favor.  The meeting was adjourned.  
Respectfully submitted by, 
Dave Di Zazzo, Chairman
